newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares seen temporarily firmer.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares seen temporarily firmer.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial shares traded largely firmer on Tuesday but brokers maintained the immediate future remained dim for equities, with fundamentals favouring a loss of investors to the local money market.
"I don't know why it's (index) going up since we still anticipate a rise in inflation and interest rates...I still think the downside is coming," one broker commented.
He said the index was probably thriving on the lingering euphoria resulting from recent good company results in a number of heavyweights.

The key industrial index added 89.73 points to close at 10,229.91, on the back of stronger deals in bankers Barclays, up 200 cents to 3,400, while hoteliers and retailers Meikles put on 40 cents to 2,650 and cement group Porthold gained 25 cents to 1,900.
Finance house udc traded 20 cents stronger at 270 and blue chip Delta and rubber product manufacturers Acacia climbed 15 cents higher to 1,725 and 190 respectively.

In minings, nickel producer Bindura and coal miners Wankie both added five cents to 805 and 565 respectively while gold company Falcon surged 200 cents to 1,400, nudging the seven-share index there 7.00 points up to 997.88.
